content.value_statement: Weak subject lines can waste email test cells and obscure a useful offer. This skill creates and ranks subject and preheader variants with clear heuristic flags before a campaign test.
actual_capabilities: Generates three to eight subject and preheader variants with stable IDs and angle labels.
Counts subject and preheader characters for desktop and mobile truncation checks.
Flags common subject-level spam patterns, including all-caps runs and deceptive prefixes.
Counts emojis and applies different guidance for promotional and cold-outbound emails.
Renders from-name, subject, and preheader as an estimated inbox preview.
Ranks variants and explains which candidates should advance to testing.
limitations: It provides heuristic flags, not mailbox-provider inbox-placement decisions.
It does not write email body copy, CTAs, or complete deliverability audits.
It cannot validate claims, prices, discounts, or scarcity without user-provided evidence.
Inbox rendering varies by email client, device, and recipient settings.

use_cases.title: Prepare a promotion test
use_cases.description: Create and rank subject and preheader options before a promotional campaign test.

use_cases.title: Review cold outreach
use_cases.description: Check B2B outreach subjects for truncation, emoji use, and misleading patterns.

use_cases.title: Improve a newsletter launch
use_cases.description: Compare newsletter subject options and preview the recipient inbox view.

prompt_templates.title: Check one subject line
prompt_templates.prompt: Pre-score this subject line and preheader for a newsletter: [subject] / [preheader]. From-name: [name].

prompt_templates.title: Generate promotion options
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate five subject-line and preheader variants for [offer] in promo mode. Use from-name [name] and rank them by heuristic pre-score.

prompt_templates.title: Review candidate list
prompt_templates.prompt: Pre-score these six subject lines for desktop and mobile truncation, spam patterns, emoji count, and inbox preview. Mode: [promo or cold]. From-name: [name]. Candidates: [list].

prompt_templates.title: Create a test-ready shortlist
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate eight distinct subject and preheader variants for [offer]. Use [promo, cold, or newsletter] mode. Mark measured and estimated checks, cut weak options, and provide a ranked shortlist for an A/B test.

output_examples.input: Generate options for a summer course discount in promo mode.
output: SUBJ-A — Benefit: Build job-ready skills this summer
Preheader: Choose a course and start learning this week.
Rank: Advance SUBJ-A. The promise appears before the estimated mobile cutoff.
Flag: Exclamation stacking and multiple emojis.
Flag: The urgency and discount require user-provided support.
Recommendation: Cut or revise before testing.

best_practices: Provide the offer, audience, mode, and from-name before generating variants.
Treat spam and truncation results as estimates, then validate with campaign results.
Use one variable per test cell after selecting the ranked shortlist.
anti_patterns: Do not present a clean heuristic pre-score as an inbox-placement guarantee.
Do not invent discounts, statistics, scarcity, or personalization claims.
Do not use this skill as a substitute for body-copy review or full deliverability testing.

faq.question: Does this skill guarantee inbox placement?
faq.answer: No. It flags common subject-level patterns but cannot predict Gmail, Outlook, or other provider decisions.

faq.question: Can it write email body copy?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on subject lines and preheaders only.

faq.question: How many variants does it create?
faq.answer: It creates three to eight variants when generating from an offer or angle.

faq.question: Can I use past campaign data?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide a manual export to inform angle and length choices. Treat results as context, not proof.

faq.question: Does it support cold outreach?
faq.answer: Yes. It applies stricter emoji guidance for B2B cold-outbound mode.

faq.question: What should I do after selecting variants?
faq.answer: Use an email experiment design process to test the surviving variants with controlled variables.
